Abstract:Mesoscale air-sea interaction occurs throughout strong sea surface temperature fronts such as the the Kuroshio Extension, but its strength is highly non-uniform and can be resolved only in kilometre-scale coupled simulations. Abstract:Systems for modular, declarative and compositional specification for data visualizations, otherwise known as visualization grammars, often claim Wilkinson’s Grammar of Graphics as motivation, inspiration or foundation. The strongest model, GPT-5.6 Sol, achieves an overall score of only 41.63%, with cross-modal EEG alignment emerging as a major bottleneck. We further examine model behavior from a neurophysiological perspective and analyze how temporal, spectral, spatial, and physiological EEG structure relates to model successes and failures. Inference-time neurophysiological guidance can reshape model predictions by helping models recognize the neurophysiological patterns present in the input and connect them with relevant neurological knowledge, narrowing the gap between general multimodal competence and EEG understanding. EEGProbe provides a testbed for current VLMs and a basis for developing future multimodal models that can interpret EEG evidence more reliably. [HC-16] UIAnchor: Anchoring UI Perception and Action Execution for Reliable Service-Composed Mobile Task Automation with GUI Agents

Abstract:Mobile task automation aims to streamline multi-step, cross-app interactions on smartphones and in-vehicle systems. Recent LLM-based GUI agents have advanced rapidly, yet reliability remains limited because modern mobile workflows are increasingly service-composed (app switching, forms, pop-ups/permissions, copy-paste), requiring fine-grained operations on dense, dynamic, and heterogeneous UIs, often in distraction-sensitive contexts (e.g., hands-busy or attention-limited use). Through an in-the-wild failure analysis of deployable GUI agents, we identify two dominant bottlenecks: agents often miss or misread actionable UI elements, and they execute actions without verifying target correctness or outcomes. We present UIAnchor, a modular multi-agent system that improves mobile GUI automation by anchoring both perception and execution. UIAnchor combines a two-stage UI parser for high-recall element capture and context-aware semantics with a meta-controller that performs pre-action verification, post-action outcome perception, per-step state tracking, and targeted recovery. We further introduce an L1-L5 task taxonomy based on step length, cross-app scope, and UI granularity, showing that L5 remains beyond today’s practical frontier. On the hardest practical tier, L4 tasks (20-30 steps, multi-app, targets 100 x 100 px, ~5 mm on typical phones), UIAnchor improves success by 31.5% over GPT-4o and 16.6% over Mobile-Agent-v3. With edge/cloud assistance, UIAnchor runs at ~2 s per step, comparable to human operation, while reducing per-step latency by up to 75.5% and energy by 52.4%. It also generalizes to unseen apps and cross-platform GUIs.

Abstract:Large language models can generate code based on natural language prompts, opening up new possibilities for users to customize software and extend its functionality. This paper proposes and implements Injectra, a general-purpose code injection and feature enhancement system for existing desktop clients, suitable for applications whose user interfaces are built using embedded browser engines (such as Electron) or system WebViews (such as Tauri). Injectra decouples the host integration logic from the upper-layer enhancement code. Combining both runtime integration and pre-launch bootstrap mechanisms, it injects JavaScript, HTML, and CSS into the application’s internal Web runtime environment through a unified execution channel, thereby enabling modifications to interface rendering, adjustments to interactive behaviors, and client-side functionality extensions. The system uses a command-line interface (CLI) as a unified entry point, allowing external tools, AI agents, and MCP integration layers to reuse its injection and enhancement capabilities. We tested 38 desktop applications already installed on our macOS machine; code injection was successfully completed for all of them. We demonstrated the system’s capability to extend functionality through various enhanced use cases and also successfully validated the Windows version. Based on Injectra, we further developed an LLM-powered enhancement tool driven by selection and annotation: users select interface objects within the original application and describe their modification requirements; the large language model then generates the enhancement code, which is injected, executed, and rendered by Injectra. Abstract:Designers share many AI tools, yet their roles produce different work. This survey compared 337 Product, Industrial and UX/UI Designers from 40 countries and regions across the four phases of the Double Diamond. It measured AI adoption, breadth and frequency, tool function and the number of tools named per phase. A tool was loyal when a role picked it in all four phases. Industrial Designers adopted AI less often (73.9% against 88.2% and 87.9%), a gap that went with physical projects once project type and country were held constant. Of 60 AI tools, 25 were common to all three roles and carried at least 90% of each role’s picks. Tool function differed by role, most of all in Develop. A few loyal tools carried about half of the picks, led by ChatGPT. Tool counts fell across the phases in every role. A hurdle model found a Phase x Role interaction for using AI in a phase (p = 0.041), which was not shown for the number of tools (p = 0.080). Predicted adoption among UX/UI Designers fell from 87.2% in Define to 43.9% in Develop. Support for designers needs one shared core, role-specific tools and most attention in Develop.

作者: Yerin Nam,Minkyung Cho,MinKyu Kim,SeungWoo Song,Hangyeol Yoo,Jihyo Kim,KyungTae Lim

Abstract:GUI agents are increasingly evaluated by whether they complete web tasks, but surface success can hide a critical failure: the final answer may not be supported by evidence observed during navigation. We introduce EVIDENT, an evidence-driven benchmark for evaluating whether GUI agents ground their decisions in observable web evidence. EVIDENT contains 220 real-world English and Korean tasks spanning semantic grounding, contextual inference, and visual grounding, each paired with human-curated evidence metadata specifying what must be verified. We further separate surface task completion from evidence-grounded success using three metrics: TSR, ESR, and GSR, which respectively measure outcome success, required evidence observation, and claim-level evidence support. Experiments on commercial and open-source GUI agents reveal substantial gaps between surface success and evidence-grounded success, especially in contextual and visual tasks. These results show that current evaluations can overestimate agent reliability and highlight the need to assess not only whether agents answer, but whether they verify.

Abstract:Human pose-driven visual effects offer a compelling way for enhancing video expressiveness and storytelling. Authoring such effects with traditional video editing tools is a complex and time-consuming task that requires considerable technical expertise and manual effort. While generative AI models can simplify the workflow by reducing manual scripting through language-driven generation, existing approaches suffer from imprecise alignment between visual effects and pose data, failure to preserve original video content, and limited support for fine-grained, iterative refinement. To address these challenges, we present PromptPoseFX, an interactive system that allows creators to author pose-driven visual effects through augmented language prompts and interactive refinement. Our system leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to translate high-level user intent into parameterized procedural graphics scripts, automatically mapping pose-tracking data to specific effect parameters, allowing precise alignment with human motion. This script-based approach manages effects as independent layers, thereby preserving the original content of the underlying video. To reduce language ambiguity, our interface offers controls across spatial, temporal, and parameter domains, enabling the precise, intuitive, and iterative authoring of pose-driven visual effects. We evaluated PromptPoseFX through a comparative study against a text-only LLM interface, followed by an exploratory study. In the comparative study, participants rated PromptPoseFX significantly higher than the text-only baseline on measures of perceived control and precision. The exploratory study examined usability and creativity support in open-ended authoring tasks.

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20375
作者: Modhumonty Das,Nathan Morelli,Aakash Gautam

Abstract:Future-planning tools often treat agency as individual and leave out the institutional conditions that shape how aspirations become action. We examine this tension in the context of reentry from incarceration and recovery from substance use disorder, through a partnership with a nonprofit organization. Building on participants’ physical vision-board practices, we designed a digital future-envisioning tool that helps users represent current circumstances, desired futures, and pathways that connect goals to concrete resources. We draw on data from three workshops involving 18 participants and follow-up interviews with 10 participants to examine how they used future envisioning within a fragmented support system. Participants described reentry and recovery as ongoing processes in which the everyday work of staying stable was central to progress. Envisioning futures supported this work by surfacing constraints and interdependencies, by reframing personal strengths and institutional supports as assets, and by helping participants move from abstract hopes toward articulated goals and contingent plans. We theorize revision as maintenance work and conclude with design implications for community-embedded interactive systems that support revisable, dependency-aware planning.

Abstract:Conversational artificial intelligence can reproduce many instructional and social behaviors of human tutors, but students may interpret those behaviors differently depending on who they believe is providing them. We examined how perceived tutor identity shapes students’ evaluations of instructional feedback, satisfaction of psychological needs according to Self-Determination Theory, and their communication strategies with tutors. In a within-subjects Wizard-of-Oz study, 27 introductory computer science students completed two text-based tutoring sessions involving Python code-explanation problems. Participants were told one tutor was human and the other was AI, although the same human provided feedback in both conditions. We found participants evaluated both tutors favorably and reported few consistent differences in the instructional value of the feedback. However, participants frequently questioned whether AI could genuinely care about them, which corresponded with the human tutor having higher scores of relatedness need satisfaction. Human presence offered connection and accountability for some participants but introduced anxiety in others. Participants also reported communicating more casually with the human tutor and more explicitly with the AI tutor. These findings suggest complementary roles for human and AI tutoring and highlight the importance of considering psychological needs alongside instructional quality.

[HC-23] Sidewalk Stewards: A Visual Analytics Approach for Interactive Topology Repair of Sidewalk Networks

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20330

Abstract:Accurate pedestrian network data is foundational to urban accessibility, routing, and infrastructure planning, yet such data remains scarce and difficult to produce at scale. Automated extraction pipelines have made significant strides by leveraging computer vision to derive sidewalk networks from aerial imagery, and have seen real-world adoption by municipalities seeking cost-effective inventory solutions. Yet, these pipelines consistently produce topological errors (e.g., disconnected components, dangling edges, missed connections, malformed intersections) that undermine the utility of the extracted networks for routing and accessibility analysis. Correcting these errors requires situated human judgment that global automated repair strategies cannot replicate, yet practitioners currently lack dedicated tools to support this work efficiently. We present Sidewalk Stewards, a visual analytics system that bridges the gap between automated extraction and a deployment-ready pedestrian network. Sidewalk Stewards detects candidate topology errors, supports interactive user-guided correction through coordinated spatial views, and provides real-time quality feedback as edits are applied. We evaluate Sidewalk Stewards through a comparative user study, case studies across cities, and a quantitative evaluation. Compared with conventional workflows, the system facilitates error identification and enables faster and more complete correction. The case studies illustrate the workflow across different urban contexts, and the quantitative evaluation shows that a small number of user corrections can enhance multiple sidewalk quality metrics. Sidewalk Stewards is available at this http URL.

[HC-24] Vibe Interventions: Can Users Personalize and Iterate Their Way to Behavior Change?

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20315

类目: Human-Computer Interaction (cs.HC)

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Recent advances in large language models allow a working application to be generated from natural-language description, and is referred to as generative user interfaces. Their application to behavior change is unexplored, and we provide one of the first controlled investigations of it. We distinguish two components of authorship: iteration, the revision of a generated artifact in natural language, and personalization, the conditioning of generation on stated context. In a pre-registered between-subjects experiment (N = 300, 60 per condition), we crossed these two factors and added a static intervention as a control, yielding five conditions; participants stated a goal and received a generated intervention. The personalized generative condition ranked highest on every self-report outcome, including ownership, satisfaction, and intended adoption. Randomized iteration had no detectable effect, and higher revision counts were negatively associated with evaluative ratings. This work establishes which component of authorship carries motivational value in generative behavior change tools.

Abstract:Urban sensing initiatives increasingly produce multimodal datasets that combine visual and textual information to capture city characteristics and subjective factors such as safety, comfort, and accessibility. Yet, analyzing such data at scale remains difficult, as manual inspection is unfeasible and automated methods struggle to interpret subjective cues and uncover relationships across diverse data modalities. Moreover, existing workflows rarely make exploration steps explicit, hindering reproducibility. To address these challenges, we introduce Reveal, a provenance-aware visual analytics system for exploring heterogeneous urban data. Reveal enables users to build dataflows by combining text and image searches across coordinated views, chaining queries into pipelines, and applying set operations within an exploration diagram while capturing analytical provenance. Abstract:Extended reality (XR) allows designers to sketch shapes directly in 3D, but converting these sketches into editable, feature-based CAD requires interpreting their intent. A sketch may contain drawing errors, intended features, and design choices that remain open. Correcting every irregularity risks erasing intended features, while automatic completion may impose choices the designer has not made. We argue that AI should add precision without overriding design intent, considering both the resulting shape and how the CAD model behaves during later edits. To guide this process, we propose a conceptual framework that distinguishes errors from intentions in individual sketch properties and relates them to correction, preservation, and exploration in editable CAD. We also outline five research directions for sketch interpretation, CAD construction, and evaluation, with testable hypotheses for selected questions.

[HC-27] DoF-Query Transformer for Adaptive Fusion of Egocentric Vision and Forearm HD-sEMG in Continuous Hand Kinematics

Abstract:Continuous and accurate estimation of human hand kinematics is important not only for intuitive human-machine interaction, but also for capturing fine-grained human manipulation demonstrations that can provide action supervision for embodied-intelligence datasets and dexterous robot learning. However, individual sensing modalities may be insufficient for reliable estimation under varying operating conditions. We present a finger-unencumbered multimodal framework for continuous regression of 20 hand joint angles from egocentric RGB images and 128-channel forearm high-density surface electromyography (HD-sEMG). The framework combines a Vision Transformer-based visual encoder, a Transformer-based EMG encoder, and a degree of freedom (DoF) query Transformer fusion decoder. To account for the varying informativeness of visual and EMG cues across joint DoFs and input conditions, the decoder assigns a separate learnable query to each DoF, enabling DoF-specific and context-adaptive fusion of the two modalities. The framework was evaluated on synchronized multimodal data from 10 participants. Averaged across participants, the proposed fusion model achieved a mean coefficient of determination ( R^2 ) of 0.88 and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 2.80^\circ , compared with 0.82 and 3.21^\circ for the vision-only model and 0.68 and 5.13^\circ for the EMG-only model. It also outperformed the evaluated representative unimodal baselines and alternative fusion designs. DoF-wise analyses showed larger fusion gains for visually ambiguous joints and viewing conditions, while synthetic visual occlusion demonstrated greater robustness than vision-only estimation. These results highlight the complementary value of egocentric vision and forearm HD-sEMG for capturing fine-grained human hand kinematics, with potential applications in human demonstration acquisition and dexterous robot learning.

Abstract:Line is a foundational building block in visual design for traditional media and computer graphics. Abstract:The CAPSARII project advances a cyber-secure, ultra-low-power wearable platform and Internet of Battlefield Things (IoBT) framework to support real-time monitoring of military personnel and data-driven decision support. The architecture integrates smart-textile sensing, a body/squad area mesh, edge-deployed AI on secure RISC-V microcontrollers, and cloud/federated analytics for cross-mission learning and comparative studies. Two representative use cases–pilot fatigue and warfighters operating in harsh environments–guide requirements, validation, and interface design (including HUD and haptic feedback). As an initial step toward embedded models, we benchmark stress classification on a public wearable dataset: tree-ensemble baselines achieve state-of-the-art performance for accuracy and F1 (e.g., XGBoost: \mathrmAccuracy=0.901!\pm!0.023 , \mathrmF1=0.920!\pm!0.019 ), while a feature-based Transformer attains the highest AUC ( 0.963!\pm!0.025 ), informing feature-engineering and compression choices for edge deployment. Building on these results, CAPSARII employs HW/SW co-design, model compression (pruning, quantization, distillation), and precision tuning to meet stringent energy and memory budgets; it further investigates Processing-in-Memory accelerators for future efficiency gains. A structured gap analysis highlights the remaining challenges: establishing validation standards for physiological signal quality and textile durability; achieving low-latency, scalable BAN/SAN communications under mobility and interference; and deploying hybrid lightweight/post-quantum cryptography with robust device identity and side-channel resilience on constrained endpoints. By consolidating these elements into a coherent, secure IoBT stack, CAPSARII delineates a practical roadmap from laboratory baselines to mission-ready soldier monitoring in both training and operational scenarios. 作者: Jialin Wang,Hai-Ning Liang
类目: Human-Computer Interaction (cs.HC)

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Tracking a decade of headset display and mass changes can inform forecasts. However, comparing headset resolution requires pixels per degree (PPD), which is often unreported and estimated using unclear assumptions. Therefore, we compile the open-source, evidence-linked HMD Resolution and Mass Database (HRMD) with 241 configurations from 2016–2026 and introduce structure- and axis-aware robust calibration (SARC) to estimate missing central PPD. Compared with official PPD, SARC reduces PPD estimation error from 14.8% for traditional geometric estimation to 3.2%. Based on HRMD, we introduce the Weight-Linked Headset Law (WL-Headset Law), which models PPD by year, mass, and category. The law reveals 7.4% annual PPD growth at fixed mass and category. Meanwhile, head-worn mass fell by 6.5% annually after category adjustment. At an eyeglass-like mass of 30g, the law projects average central PPD of 60 (normal visual acuity) around 2035 and 120 (higher acuity) around 2044 if trends persist.

[HC-31] urning Errors into Successes: Designing LLM Tutoring Around Scaffolded Error Correction

Abstract:Large language models (LLMs) could make personalized tutoring available at scale, but it remains unclear how they can best support the instructional processes that make one-on-one instruction effective. We compared two ways of using LLMs after students make errors: providing personalized explanations of those errors, or engaging students in additional cycles of scaffolded practice and feedback, with a Socratic tutor guiding students toward the correct answer. In a preregistered online experiment, 400 adults practiced setting up constraint equations and, after each attempt, received the correct answer, a generic explanation, a personalized LLM explanation of their error, or Socratic tutoring. Socratic tutoring helped: participants resolved 64% of their errors through the dialogue and scored 0.24 SD higher on practice-aligned posttest questions than those who received generic or personalized explanations. Socratic participants also found the session more interesting, less frustrating, and less costly, even though it took nearly twice as long. In contrast, we found no evidence of a benefit of personalized explanations over generic ones, and neither type of explanation reliably outperformed simply seeing the correct answer. These findings suggest that LLM tutors may add the most value not by explaining errors more precisely but by helping students correct those errors themselves through scaffolded practice. This pattern fits a mastery-experience account of tutoring, in which an effective tutor notices when a student is struggling, steps in with guidance, and works with the student until the struggle resolves into success. AI tutors may be most effective when designed around this principle.

Abstract:Wheelchair-mounted robotic arms can help people with limited upper-limb mobility reach and manipulate everyday objects, but operating them typically requires stepwise joystick control and frequent mode switching. Natural-language interfaces could let users express task-level goals, yet they must handle ambiguous requests, distinguish commands from nearby conversation, and support interruption. We present VoiceGuard, a voice interface that separates spoken intent from robot execution through structured request validation and a local stop mechanism. On-device detectors handle the wake phrase and stop commands, an audio-native large language model (LLM) routes each request into a structured function packet, a rule-based ToolDispatcher accepts, rejects, or clarifies the packet, and a SmolVLA vision-language-action (VLA) policy executes accepted tasks on a low-cost SO-101 arm. Preliminary tests showed that the system correctly handled 55 of 60 voice commands, including ambiguous and non-directed utterances, completed 16 of 20 deliveries, and stopped the arm on all 20 stop commands with a median latency of 210 ms. We demonstrate the feasibility of combining flexible spoken input with constrained task execution and local interruption for wheelchair-mounted assistive manipulation.

Abstract:As older adults increasingly live alone, emergency support becomes an important function for home companion robots. In Australia, demand for the care and support workforce is projected to nearly double between 2020-21 and 2049-50. Service robots such as robot dogs may support older adults by combining everyday companionship with assistance when human support is not immediately available. We present the design and implementation of a domestic companion-robot system on a Unitree Go1 quadruped platform that combines companionship with emergency awareness and response. The system uses a three-stage interaction model consisting of companion, danger-awareness, and emergency modes. A rule-based escalation policy combines signs detected from visual and speech input to determine the current risk level and adjust how long the robot waits for the user to confirm safety before entering emergency mode. Additional detected signs can shorten this waiting time. Users can confirm safety, request immediate help, stop robot motion, or reset the system. We verified the implemented decision rules and escalation timing through 105 automated trials and 25 staged physical trials. Additional visual evidence shortened the waiting time, and the system entered emergency mode when the waiting time ended without confirmation.

Abstract:While HCI has expanded from Personal to Family Informatics, researchers still lack a critical analytical vocabulary to diagnose what truly constitutes a collective care context. We introduce Sangyadhi, an analytical sociotechnical framework that synthesizes Situated Action, Distributed Cognition, the Capabilities Approach, and Actor-Network Theory to investigate multi-actor care ecologies. The framework articulates four interdependent analytical lenses: contextual grounding, distributed responsibility, trust-mediated sharing, and collaborative actionability. To demonstrate its diagnostic utility, we apply Sangyadhi to critically audit a decade of HCI digital health literature across self-tracking, family informatics, and clinical AI—surfacing structural omissions in how shifting authority, dynamic trust, and AI escalation are conceptualized. Ultimately, the goal of Sangyadhi is to equip researchers with an analytical blueprint for diagnosing observed care contexts, structuring field inquiries, and evaluating future technologies.

Abstract:Health management is often a collective activity, involving family members and close relations in monitoring, interpreting, and coordinating care. Abstract:Cyber-physical-human systems close a loop around people by sensing human behavior, predict it and act on it. Formally, ANCHOR is a switched port-Hamiltonian system with 52 parameters, and each part stands for a testable claim from team psychology. Because of this structure, for any fitted parameters, a forecast moves away from rest only when task progress or a prompt pushes it, and prompts of bounded size that are spaced in time move it a bounded distance. On \nGroups four-person teams held out from training, a team that drifts from its usual behavior returns most of the way within half a minute. After 32 s, about 24% of the deviation remains, and ANCHOR predicted 30%. Forecasts are clearly better when the resting point blends its three sources than when it uses one. ANCHOR matches the accuracy of a black-box baseline with about 40,000 parameters. It anticipates conversation collapse with an AUROC of 0.85. 作者: Huawei Lin,Jinting Liu,Tongyan Wang,Xuyang Chen,Ruihua Shi,Zhichao Xu,Jiaxin Qin,Guoshenghui Zhao,Baijian Yang,Yingjie Victor Chen,Tan Yu,Weijie Zhao
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)
备注: 74 pages, 11 figures, 26 tables. Code: this https URL

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Visual agents answer questions about ultra-high-resolution photos by zooming into the relevant regions. However, existing agents often answer from common sense instead of reading the evidence. Reinforcement learning (RL) on the final answer cannot correct this, because a guess earns the same reward as reading. We propose Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization (CrossRPO), which trains agents on contrast sets. A contrast set asks one question about several versions of an image that differ only in a small region with the evidence and have different answers, so only reading the evidence solves the whole set. CrossRPO rewards solving the whole set, and we prove that it does not reinforce a set answered from common sense. We build contrast sets for training (ViRA-Train) and evaluation (ViRA-Bench) by editing one small object in images of 21 to 120 megapixels, and we photograph further sets with real changes (ViRA-Bench-Real) to exclude editing traces. We train two Visual Reasoning Agents, ViRA-9B and ViRA-27B, with CrossRPO on only about 3,500 items of ViRA-Train each. CrossRPO achieves 63.3% set accuracy on ViRA-Bench at the maximum resolution, against 59.3% for GRPO. ViRA-9B is the most accurate open model of its size on all benchmarks, and ViRA-27B outperforms Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6-Luna, both at their highest thinking level, on most benchmarks.

[CV-1] FaceJev: Direct Visual Decisions for Face Forgery Detection

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21604
作者: Siran Peng,Tianshuo Zhang,Yibo Xue,Ajian Liu,Haoyuan Zhang,Weisong Zhao,Shuhuan Chen,Xiangyu Zhu,Zhen Lei
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Face forgery detection methods often perform well on seen manipulations but generalize poorly to unseen ones. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can recognize facial parts and assess their visual plausibility. Existing MLLM-based methods typically express these judgments through textual explanations, but seldom treat individual part decisions as explicit learning targets. We present FaceJev, an MLLM-based method for face forgery detection through direct visual decisions. Following the Jev formulation, FaceJev answers eight independent questions about facial parts using a shared image encoding and reads anomaly probabilities from the native answer logits. A face is classified as forged if any part is predicted to be abnormal, directly linking the detection result to the part decisions. We construct PartForensics, a dataset of approximately 160k images with binary anomaly targets for the eight facial parts, to supervise these decisions. We further propose FS-GRPO, which optimizes each part decision through an exact reward comparison with its alternative, using both detection and part rewards. FaceJev outperforms the strongest baseline by 7.25 percentage points on unseen manipulations. Extensive ablation studies validate our design choices and the effectiveness of the main components.

[CV-2] When Do Histology Foundation Models Need Geometric Test-Time Augmentation?

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21565
作者: Lars Chen,Valentino F. Foit,Dorry Segev,Michal Mankowski
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Machine Learning (cs.LG)
备注: 17 pages, 5 figures

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Test-time augmentation (TTA) aggregates model predictions across multiple transformed views of an input during inference. Because histology images lack a canonical orientation, D_4 TTA—pooling across the 8 rotations and reflections of a square—is a standard default in computational pathology. However, the rise of self-supervised histology foundation models (FMs) with inherent rotational invariance calls its continued utility into question. We benchmark 9 histology FMs and 6 general-purpose models across four patch-level and two whole-slide image (WSI) datasets. We find that D_4 TTA remains a reliable post hoc improvement, but benefits diminish from +1.98 percentage points (pp) for general-purpose backbones to +0.50 pp for histology FMs on TCGA-UT, and shrink further for the largest models. To eliminate computational overhead, our experiments demonstrate that entropy routing—applying TTA selectively to uncertain predictions—recovers most of the gain while augmenting only \sim13% of samples. Finally, we show that patch-level TTA improvements do not transfer to slide-level multiple instance learning (MIL). Code: this https URL

[CV-3] Wildfire-SSR: Geolocation-Aware Multimodal Fusion for Structure-Level Wildfire Risk Assessment

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21563
作者: Yu-Hsuan Ho,Yiming Xiao,Hao-En Lai,Ali Mostafavi,Samuel D. Brody
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Structure-level wildfire vulnerability assessment is critical for reducing losses in wildland-urban interface communities, yet existing methods often fail to combine parcel-scale ignition pathways with community-scale geographic coverage. This study introduces Wildfire-SSR (Satellite and Street-view for wildfire Risk), a geolocation-aware multimodal framework that integrates macro-scale satellite context with micro-scale street-view evidence. A Vision-Language Model extracts wildfire-relevant building and site attributes from pre-event street-view panoramas and converts them into structured semantic text. These features are spatially aligned with satellite imagery through a decoupled cross-attention fusion decoder, while a frozen satellite-pretrained DINOv3 encoder captures overhead visual context. Alternative geolocation embedding strategies are evaluated to anchor text-derived features within each satellite patch. The framework is tested on approximately 37,000 structures affected by the 2025 Eaton and Palisades fires in Los Angeles, using wildfire risk labels derived from relative post-event damage patterns to better represent inherent structural vulnerability. Rotary Positional Embedding provides the strongest spatial grounding, achieving a building localization F1 score of 0.6735 and a harmonic mean F1 score of 0.2476 for five-class pixel-level risk classification, outperforming unimodal baselines and an unanchored multimodal configuration. The model also shows a conservative bias in higher-risk classes, reducing severe-risk underestimation, and completes end-to-end assessment of the study area in 37 minutes on a single GPU. Wildfire-SSR reframes cross-view fusion as localized semantic alignment and provides a scalable tool for mitigation prioritization, resilience planning, and insurance-oriented wildfire risk assessment.

[CV-4] Reference Forcing: Long Video Generation with Region-Guided Drift Correction

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21559
作者: Sheng Zhao,Haitian Zheng,Weikai Lin,Junjie Zhao,Yuhao Zhu
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 17 pages, 12 figures, 3 tables. Project page: this https URL

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Long video generation should keep the subject and background consistent while supporting rich, natural motion. However, autoregressive models are often distilled with distribution matching distillation (DMD) over short windows, which does not train them to keep this consistency over long ranges. As a result, the subject and background can drift over time. Methods that manage the key-value (KV) cache retain or retrieve history to reduce drift. Yet this history may itself have drifted. We propose Reference Forcing, which uses the initial frames as an appearance reference. We first build a teacher that uses attention masks to force each region of a new frame to attend to the same region in the initial frames. The teacher finds these regions with off-the-shelf segmentation models. We then distill this behavior into a separate attention path of the student, which needs no external models at inference. We further introduce value correction, which corrects drifted values in the KV cache toward the matching values of drift-free initial frames. Experiments show that Reference Forcing achieves state-of-the-art subject and background consistency among long-video methods on different base models, and its advantage grows with video length. Ablations show both components are needed to gain consistency without losing motion. More visualizations and code are available at this https URL

[CV-5] BLIP-Live: Balancing Timeliness Firing Precision in Proactive Streaming Video Agents

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21553
作者: Kanchana Ranasinghe,Honglu Zhou,Dominick Reilly,Le Xue,Shusheng Yang,Juan Carlos Niebles,Silvio Savarese,Ran Xu
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Streaming video understanding is becoming increasingly important for real-world interactive systems. Such systems must be proactive for natural and useful human interaction: they should respond as soon as sufficient evidence becomes available while avoiding premature, redundant, or incorrect responses. We present BLIP-Live, a framework unifying data, metrics, harness, and training around a shared formulation of proactivity as effective causal response decisions balancing the two competing objectives of responding vs silence. First, we construct BLIP-Live-780K dataset containing human annotations of proactive response content and timing, which defines this desired behavior. We then propose PAUC-F, a metric to effectively measure our desired proactive behavior. PAUC-F combines existing response timeliness metrics with firing precision to reward early useful responses without rewarding excessive firing. With our desired behavior defined and measurable, we finally investigate model-agnostic inference harnesses that draw out proactive streaming capabilities of offline vision language models (VLMs), together with training pipelines that learn to further improve their proactive responsiveness. Across both settings, we find that combinations of sliding visual windows, online interaction memory, and structured response outputs consistently yield strongest proactive performance. Our experiments result in two models, with our BLIP-Live-Qwen model achieving state-of-the-art performance across four proactive streaming benchmarks, with gains up to 44% over baselines and outperforming multiple closed API models. Our code and data will be released publicly.

[CV-6] DuoFlow: Towards Synchronized Speech and Motion Generation with Fine-Grained Control

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21530
作者: Jun Dong,Ronghui Li,Zhongyuan Hu,Yunqi Zhao,Lijie Guo,Ruizhang Xu,Di Kang,Linchao Bao,Xiu Li
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:An embodied speaker’s expressiveness depends not only on what is said, but also on how the voice sounds and how the body moves. However, existing joint speech-motion generation models are largely driven implicitly by transcript semantics or intermediate speech representations, offering little explicit control over motion hierarchy, body parts, or vocal style. To bridge this gap, we construct MotionSpeech, a structured benchmark for controllable joint speech-motion generation that includes transcripts, voice-style descriptions, and motion conditions at two hierarchical levels. Building on this benchmark, we propose DuoFlow, a dual-stream latent flow transformer that jointly denoises speech and motion under a shared noise level and a unified second-based temporal coordinate. Modality-specific residual connectors inject structured conditions into the corresponding streams, layer-wise bidirectional cross-modal attention coordinates their generation, and a monotonic phoneme pathway combines normalized progress anchors with CTC supervision to strengthen speech temporal modeling. DuoFlow provides a unified interface for fine-grained motion and vocal-style control and demonstrates the ability to synthesize high-quality, synchronized, and instruction-consistent speech-motion sequences.

[CV-7] GHySSeg: Real-Time Geometric Ground and Road Segmentation for Hybrid Solid-State LiDAR

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21507
作者: Martín Palos,Fernando García
类目: Robotics (cs.RO); Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 14 pages, 8 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible. HySoLiD-Drive dataset: this https URL

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Hybrid solid-state LiDAR sensors are making their way into production vehicles, yet the data they produce differs structurally from that of the established spinning mechanical sensors behind today’s autonomous-driving datasets: it is ring-free, dense, cluttered, and concentrated in a frontal field of view. The classical geometric methods that autonomous vehicles rely on for drivable space computation and navigation assume the ordered ring-and-column structure of a 360-degree spinning LiDAR and degrade or fail on this data, while learned alternatives are computationally heavy, hard to certify, and trained almost exclusively on spinning-LiDAR data. We demonstrate that the same dense, per-curve geometry is instead an opportunity to close the divide between the industry’s preferred sensors and autonomous-driving research. We present GHySSeg, a purely geometric method that segments ground and drivable road from a single hybrid solid-state LiDAR frame by tracing each scan curve and reading two geometric signatures, a step in height and a fold-back in range, with no training and no graphics processing unit. To evaluate it, we release HySoLiD-Drive, the first public benchmark dedicated to ground and road segmentation on an automotive hybrid solid-state LiDAR, comprising 100 manually labeled and 7000 unlabeled frames recorded by two vehicles in real driving. On this benchmark, GHySSeg surpasses both geometric and learned state-of-the-art baselines across ground and road segmentation, reaching an intersection-over-union of 0.907 for road and 0.896 for ground at over 0.96 precision, while running in real time at about 22 milliseconds per frame on a single core.

[CV-8] Lost in the Hallway: Benchmarking Persistent Spatial Memory Across Revisits

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21485
作者: Henry Zheng,Weibo Gong,Yang Yue,Rui Huang,Yang Zhang,Gao Huang
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Persistent spatial understanding is essential for embodied agents to operate reliably in environments they repeatedly encounter. It requires recognizing revisited places despite viewpoint changes, distinguishing them from similar-looking rooms, and updating memories as environments change. Yet existing evaluations often leave physical place identity across separated visits implicit. We introduce ReSpaceBench, a benchmark comprising 3,244 questions across 590 synthetic and real-home scenes, organized into 9 tasks spanning room association, persistent state tracking, and downstream reasoning. Controlled walkthroughs define visits by physical room entry and deliberately include same-type room distractors and cross-session object changes. Our evaluation of 32 models and 3 agentic video-understanding frameworks reveals substantial limitations: the strongest evaluated zero-shot model achieves 50.5% overall accuracy and 52.2% on a 450-question subset, compared with 90.1% for human annotators. The evaluated agentic frameworks offer no overall improvement over direct inference with the same base model. Analysis of agent execution traces reveals evidence omissions and incorrect cross-visit room associations as major failure modes, suggesting that iterative evidence seeking alone does not ensure consistent spatial memory. Further analyses expose a gap between recognizing familiar rooms and identifying the correct visited room, while annotation-guided sampling highlights the importance of preserving intervening visits and transitions. We also provide RS-30K, a separate training dataset from synthetic sources with no template, scene, route, or video overlap with the benchmark. Fine-tuning Qwen3-VL-8B raises overall accuracy from 35.5% to 60.4%, with the largest gains in association and improvements extending to real-life scenes.

[CV-9] LynnReal-Hand: Unlocking World Interaction with Hand Control

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21479
作者: Shaohao Rui,Chaoyang Zhang,Xiaofeng Mao,Weijie Ma
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Interactive video world models enable exploration through text and camera controls, yet direct object interaction requires finer control. Hands provide a natural interface, but translating continuous hand movements into coherent visual responses remains challenging because of complex hand-object dynamics and demanding real-time computation. To address these challenges, we introduce LynnReal-Hand, a hand-controlled video world model that unifies precise interaction modeling with efficient streaming generation. We curate 100K interaction clips spanning diverse real and synthetic environments and develop hand-aware supervision to improve fine-grained hand motions and object interactions. Building on this foundation, we learn a causal flow map for few-step generation and introduce region-aware score distillation that combines complementary video and image priors to refine interaction dynamics and visual appearance. To further reduce inference latency, we propose Ultra-Fast-VAE, a compact video decoder that preserves high reconstruction fidelity with substantially lower computational cost. Extensive evaluations on HandBench demonstrate superior hand-following accuracy and visual quality compared with existing approaches. Our full-sequence model achieves an FVD of 181.67 and a MANO Dice score of 93.02, while the three-step causal model maintains a MANO Dice score of 92.49. For real-time interaction, 540p streaming on a single H200 reaches 18.03 FPS with 741ms latency and an optimized peak GPU memory footprint of only 34.89GB. We will release the datasets, model weights, and the full training and inference code to support research on hand-controlled video world models.

[CV-10] Event-Triggered Visual Perception for Real-Time Harvest Outcome Estimation in Mechanical Blueberry Harvesting

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21472
作者: Nicolas Miroslav Husár,Jelle Driessen,Petra Bosilj,Başak Sakçak
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Mechanical blueberry harvesting requires a balance between removing ripe fruit and avoiding premature removal of unripe berries that could remain on the bush for a later harvest. However, operators generally lack real-time information about the maturity composition of the fruit being collected. This study develops an event-triggered machine-vision system that measures the maturity of harvested blueberries directly on the harvester. When a filled crate is moved by the machine, an RGB image is automatically captured and analysed using a three-class detector that identifies ripe, semi-ripe, and unripe berries. The system operates locally on the existing CPU-only industrial computer and therefore requires neither continuous image processing nor dedicated GPU hardware. During field testing, 79 crate images containing 48,634 visible blueberries in manually verified reference annotations were evaluated. The vision system estimated an overall ripe-fruit fraction of 90.22%, compared with 90.97% determined manually. Per-image ripe-fruit estimates showed a mean absolute error of 0.935 percentage points and a Pearson correlation of r=0.967. Maturity estimates remained similar between the two sides of the harvester for which the light conditions varied despite poorer absolute counting performance under direct sunlight. All field events were processed within the available 14 s per-side crate interval. The proposed approach provides a practical means of quantifying one component of harvest selectivity while the machine is operating. Such information could support operator decision-making and, when combined with measurements of fruit recovery and losses, contribute to future feedback-based control of mechanical harvesting.

[CV-11] Out of Sight Into Memory: Compact Visual Latents Retain Local Evidence in Ultra-High-Resolution Remote Sensing

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21457
作者: Meng Tang,Siyuan Du,Yuxin Liu,Shuaishuai Cao,Di Wang,Haonan Guo
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Question answering over ultra-high-resolution (UHR) remote sensing scenes poses a tension for multimodal large language models: global overviews obscure small objects and local attributes, whereas detailed crops consume substantial context. Compressing inspected crops into short sequences of continuous visual latents offers a compact memory once crop tokens are discarded, yet diagnostic studies on natural images find that models often ignore latent content, leaving unclear whether compact latents can retain fine-grained targets lost in downsampled UHR remote sensing scenes. To isolate evidence retention from region selection, we encode high-resolution crops into latent memory tokens for frozen backbones and evaluate both their predictive utility and content dependence. Across two generations of Qwen-VL on LRS-GRO, a 64-token memory achieves 7.6- to 9.9-fold compression of retained crop tokens and improves accuracy by 2.5 to 4.8 percentage points over the downsampled global image alone, recovering most of the high-resolution crop gain with consistent behavior on XLRS-Bench. Substituting memory from another image or another region of the same scene reduces accuracy by 5.8 to 7.4 percentage points and yields lower accuracy than removing memory altogether, demonstrating that predictions depend on the encoded regional evidence. Restoring the source crop within the same model reduces the accuracy loss caused by zeroing or removing memory. These findings establish that compact visual latents retain useful local evidence in UHR remote sensing and identify evidence availability as a key factor governing their contribution.

[CV-12] [CLS] and [EOS] Tokens are not Enough for CLIP-based Class-Incremental Learning

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21440
作者: Hao Sun,Tao Hu,Shixiong Kai,Siyuan Xu,Wenqian Zhao,Mingxuan Yuan,Da-Wei Zhou
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: Accepted to TMM. Code is available at: this https URL

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Class-Incremental Learning (CIL) aims to empower models to continuously acquire new knowledge while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. With the advent of vision-language models like CLIP, leveraging their cross-modal alignment capabilities to address CIL challenges has emerged as a dominant paradigm. Existing methods leverage CLIP’s global representations (i.e., the visual [CLS] token and the textual [EOS] token) for cross-modal alignment. While achieving effective classification, they overlook the rich patch-level visual features and token-level textual semantics inherent in CLIP. For example, the [CLS] token aggregates local information to capture the general concept of “cat”, while the patch-level details retain specific localized features essential for recognition, such as the tail, fur, and face. We propose PACE (PAtch-token Cross-modal Enhancement) to uncover the long-neglected local representations within CLIP. First, based on the global representations like [CLS] token and [EOS] token, we identify the top-k most crucial visual patches and textual tokens. Subsequently, to better utilize the extracted key local features, we design a cross-modal fusion module. This module leverages local textual semantics to refine visual representations, while augmenting textual semantics with local visual features. As the fusion module is shared across all tasks, directly fine-tuning it on new tasks would interfere with the knowledge learned from previous tasks, leading to catastrophic forgetting. To alleviate this, we employ a projection-based update strategy to effectively preserve the critical parameter space of previous tasks during the adaptation to new tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PACE significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple CIL benchmarks.

[CV-13] Power Line Detection in Point Clouds with Point-SAM and RANSAC

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21438
作者: Christoph Dalitz,Oskar Waedt,Steffen Goebbels,Mahdieh Shamsadini Motlagh,Gabriel Gerzabek
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 8 pages, 10 figures, accepted for VISAPP 2027

点击查看摘要

Abstract:This article deals with the problem of detecting the position of power lines in airborne laser scanning point clouds. We address both the problem of segmenting power lines from background like ground and vegetation and of identifying individual lines. For segmentation we compare a rule-based approach with one based on transfer learning (Point-SAM). For individual line detection, we derive the mathematical formulas for RANSAC applied to 3D catenaries and compare it with a non-parametric method (TriplClust). All methods are evaluated on a newly created dataset “PowLiDFR”, which we make publicly available. The samples have been taken from the French project LiDAR HD and cover a variety of terrain layouts and point cloud resolutions. On this dataset, an unsupervised transfer learning outperformed a mere rule-based segmentation, and for individual power line detection, RANSAC was better in following the shape of catenaries than the non-parametric algorithm.

[CV-14] Quality and Similarity Indicators for Video-Based Heart Rate and Respiratory Rate Fusion: A Controlled Evaluation

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21419
作者: Nhi Nguyen,Le Nguyen,Manuel Lage Cañellas,Miguel Bordallo López,Constantino Álvarez Casado
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 15 pages, 7 figures, 4 tables; with 14 pages supplementary material included

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Camera-based heart rate (HR) and respiratory rate (RR) estimates vary in reliability from window to window, and a common remedy is to fuse several extraction methods with weights from reference-free signal quality indicators. However, few studies test whether these indicators identify the most accurate method in each window or outperform simpler fusion. We evaluate 11 quality indicators and 8 inter-method similarity measures for fusing 7 HR and 10 RR extractors on four public datasets (75 test subjects). Filters, indicator directions, weighting parameters and a learned ridge baseline are selected on a separate five-subject set before testing. Fusion is compared with equal averaging, a constant typical-rate predictor, the best single method selected in advance and in hindsight, and a per-window oracle with a permutation-based null, using subject-level bootstrap confidence intervals. For HR, quality-weighted fusion reduced mean absolute error by 10.9% [5.2, 18.4] relative to averaging and by 15.6% [8.1, 23.1] relative to the method selected in advance, and was statistically indistinguishable from the best method selected in hindsight. Weighting methods by their agreement did not improve on averaging. For RR, the indicators could not identify the more accurate estimates: sharpened quality weighting increased error (-2.6% [-4.8, -0.8]), fused estimates were uncorrelated with the reference (r = 0.22), and averaging was less accurate than the typical-rate predictor (-3.1% [-6.1, -0.4]). With a second respiratory reference, apparent RR gains reflected estimates moving toward its typical rate. Quality-guided fusion is worthwhile for video HR; for RR, 30-s windows improved estimates but not fusion.

[CV-15] Flexible Multi-Stack Super-Resolution of Clinical Brain MRI Using Hetero-Orientation Variational Encoding: Expert Reader Evaluation in a Nigerian Cohort

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21412
作者: Kabir Hamzah Muhammad,Lorena Garcia-Foncillas Macias,Soumya Snigdha Kundu,Emily Guilhem,Jon Cleary,Amal Saleh Nour,Yodit Abraham Yaynishet,Chinasa Kalaiwo,Peter Chibuta,Ugumba Kwikima,Udunna Anazodo,Jonathan Shapey,Tom Vercauteren
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 27 pages, 14 figures

点击查看摘要

Abstract:High-resolution brain MRI is important for neuroradiological assessment, yet routine clinical protocols often rely on fast, anisotropic 2D acquisitions, particularly in resource-constrained settings. These acquisitions may differ in orientation, alignment and anatomical coverage, resulting in partially overlapping image stacks. Existing learning-based super-resolution methods typically rely on single, under-constrained inputs or fixed multi-stack configurations with idealised acquisition geometry. We introduce MS-HVED, a sequence-agnostic framework for flexible multi-stack brain MRI super-resolution. Available axial, coronal and sagittal stacks are independently encoded into multi-scale Gaussian posteriors and fused using a field-of-view-aware Product-of-Gaussians formulation that limits contributions from unsupported regions. Physics-informed domain randomisation simulates heterogeneous clinical acquisition conditions, including obliqueness, partial coverage and imaging artefacts. MS-HVED achieved competitive or superior reconstruction fidelity across synthetic benchmarks and improved downstream tissue segmentation relative to low-resolution inputs. To assess generalisation beyond the training cohorts, we performed external clinical validation on 30 routine brain MRI examinations from a Nigerian cohort, representing an under-represented population in medical imaging research. These examinations formed the largest component of a blinded reader study involving 44 real cases and seven expert neuroradiologists. In the Nigerian cohort, MS-HVED was preferred over the supervised baseline for overall image quality in 187 of 210 paired assessments. Across all clinical cohorts, MS-HVED achieved higher overall-quality scores with all available inputs (5.93 vs. 4.49, p.001), with the preference persisting when axial or coronal inputs were omitted (p.001). [CV-16] Portrait Fitness as a Pretext: Probing Implicit Demographic Bias in VLMs WACV2027

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21403
作者: Alexandre Fournier-Montgieux,Akram Elbouanani,Aboubacar Tuo,Adrian Popescu,Hervé Le Borgne,Bertrand Luvison
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Computers and Society (cs.CY)
备注: Accepted at WACV 2027

点击查看摘要

Abstract:We audit face-related bias in VLMs using BALPORTRAITS, a new balanced dataset of 9,000 fictional portraits across ethnicity, gender, and age segments. Sixteen VLMs estimate portrait fitness scores for occupations, brands, activities, and banking or insurance products within an advertising-casting framework designed to avoid direct inference of protected attributes. Item-level estimations are aggregated with scenario-specific prestige scores to compare rankings across demographic groups. While the magnitude and direction of these biases vary across scenarios, model families, and demographic dimensions, with age, ethnicity, and gender contributing differently depending on the task, we find demographic dispersion across all evaluated models, with a majority of pairwise segment differences reaching statistical significance. This study introduces a controlled protocol to assess implicit face-related associations and demonstrates that single-scenario or single-attribute audits are insufficient.

[CV-17] VideoNexus: Video Perception Beyond the Reasoning Context

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21392
作者: Yancheng Long,Xuanyu Zheng,Wei Chen,Luoyuan Zhang,Haoyang Xu,Bin Wen,Tingting Gao
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Understanding long videos requires locating evidence, resolving visual details, and integrating observations into an answer. Even when relevant evidence is present, performing these operations within long, dense visual sequences burdens both perception and reasoning. Video agents enable selective inspection, but returning frames to the planner still accumulates visual information in its reasoning context. Delegating perception reduces this burden, yet sparse sampling can miss decisive details, and per-frame descriptions can preserve context growth. We introduce VideoNexus, a training-free framework that separates detailed video perception from evidence-driven planning and reasoning. The planner controls where to inspect, what to resolve, and how densely to sample. Perception sub-agents process native audio-video in independent contexts and return compact, temporally grounded evidence for iterative search and verification. Using Gemini 3.8 Flash for both planning and perception, VideoNexus achieves 88.6% accuracy on full LVBench, exceeding same-backbone static ingestion and built-in agentic processing by 3.6 and 1.1 points, respectively, at 44% of the latter’s measured API cost. A paired LVBench subset ablation shows lower planner input and higher accuracy. With Kimi K3 as the shared backbone, VideoNexus improves over the official Video-GAIA ReAct harness by 8.5 points in our evaluation. These results support compact evidence exchange for combining detailed observation with efficient planning and reasoning.

Abstract:3D Gaussian Splatting enables object-level operations on Gaussian primitives, yet existing segmentation methods are largely trained and evaluated through rendered views. Abstract:Streaming video generation must sustain quality beyond the training horizon while handling self-generated history and growing cache costs. Abstract:Many materials and tissues, including carbon-nanotube sheets, collagen and paper, comprise overlapping strands whose arrangement influences their effective properties. Abstract:Uncertainty quantification for novel view synthesis with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) assesses rendering reliability at unseen viewpoints. Abstract:Semi-supervised object detection has recently been extended to DETR, where oriented boxes introduce an ambiguity that does not arise for axis-aligned boxes: the map from parameters to rectangles is two-to-one, since (c_x,c_y,w,h,\theta) and (c_x,c_y,h,w,\theta+\pi/2) denote the same rotated rectangle. Losses and matching costs are computed from the parameters, so two boxes that coincide in space can be far apart in the metric that drives training. Abstract:Recent inversion-free, flow-based image editing methods evolve the source image toward the target via a differential velocity field. Abstract:Anomalies are local events, yet weakly supervised video anomaly detection scores them globally. Abstract:Weakly-supervised Video Anomaly Detection (VAD) models assign anomaly scores from high-dimensional features, and their predictions remain unexplained. Abstract:Source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) adapts a model trained on a labelled source domain to an unlabelled target domain without access to the source data. 作者: Masahiro Ryo
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)
备注: 32 pages including supplementary material; 6 numbered figures and a graphical summary

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Natural photographs contain dense, overlapping structures that can be weakly expressed in feature maps from whole-image vision encoders. We introduce forced focused attention (FFA) and its Python implementation, vividRGB. FFA is an encoder-agnostic inference-time procedure that applies a frozen encoder to enlarged, overlapping local crops, averages inverse-aligned reflections, and reconstructs a feature field in source coordinates. We evaluate 50 high-resolution photographs from grassland vegetation, fungal networks, airborne forests, coral reefs, and phytoplankton microscopy, using DINOv3 ViT-B/16. Across the five domains, FFA at 5% or 10% focus produces higher mean RGB-edge boundary F1 than direct DINOv3 encoding and automatic SAM3 masks. Domain means range from 0.244 to 0.596 for FFA, versus 0.028-0.076 for direct DINOv3 and 0.020-0.090 for SAM3. Qualitative feature maps also show finer appearance structure. These results concern RGB-edge preservation rather than verified species, traits, or biological segmentation. Narrower focus generally improves boundary preservation, while extraction time and GPU energy use increase sharply and gains diminish at finer settings. FFA may be useful for relatively small, high-resolution ecological image collections where dense visual cues matter. The alpha release vividRGB 0.1.0 and versioned research resources support reproducible cue inspection.

[CV-59] Learning What the True Labels Would Teach: Posterior Analytic Class-Incremental Learning with Unlabeled Data

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20937
作者: Wei Tang,Tong Wei,Jiahao Zhang,Min-Ling Zhang,Lijie Hu,Fakhri Karray
类目: Machine Learning (cs.LG); Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:In class-incremental learning with unlabeled data, each task brings only class names and unlabeled images, so CLIP’s zero-shot predictions replace labels. Existing methods train on hard pseudo-labels, but a wrong one gives the true class zero probability, which self-training often confirms. We argue that each image should carry its label posterior, as an analytic classifier trained on posteriors equals the true-label one in expectation. The zero-shot prediction is not this posterior, as its class proportions confound name bias with true imbalance and it ignores other images. We propose Posterior Analytic Class-Incremental Learning (PACIL), which corrects the class prior with a prior selection rule and refines each distribution by a fixed-prior von Mises-Fisher mixture on whitened features. These soft labels train the classifier and replace labels to select its fusion weight with zero-shot CLIP by closed-form leave-one-out cross-validation. We prove that posterior targets minimize the mean-square gap to the true-label prediction and that their argmax widens this gap only through ambiguous images. The fusion weight selected with soft labels loses at most their distance to the posteriors in expected correct decisions. PACIL has the best average incremental accuracy among methods trained without labels on all 18 settings.

备注: Project Page: this https URL

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Despite recent advances, vision-language models (VLMs) still struggle with fine-grained visual understanding, often failing to effectively utilize critical evidence already encoded in their visual representations. Existing approaches address this limitation through repeated visual processing or explicit reasoning, introducing substantial computational overhead. In this paper, we propose ReAccess, a lightweight framework that preserves and reuses question-relevant visual evidence through compact associative memory. Constructed during a single visual prefill, the memory supports progressive evidence retrieval that steers both attention queries and hidden representations, enabling effective visual grounding without repeated image encoding or explicit reasoning traces. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent improvements in both general visual understanding and fine-grained perception, while achieving substantially faster inference than existing reasoning-intensive approaches, demonstrating a promising path to efficient multimodal reasoning.

Abstract:Tool-handover interaction calls for preparation before a response is warranted. The model waits until interaction cues appear, then prepares while assessing whether the accumulating evidence supports a response or calls for cancellation. We introduce EviBridge, a framework that integrates predictive visual representations into a vision-language interaction model for joint state and tool prediction. A trainable evidence interface maps features from a frozen V-JEPA 2 encoder into the language decoder alongside native visual inputs, preserving their temporal context and using only observations available at each decision time. The framework has two instantiations. EviBridge-E distinguishes recent from historical evidence and encodes the timing and spatial location of each observation. EviBridge-I preserves the temporal order of pooled V-JEPA 2 features and interaction turns and generates dedicated interaction tokens. We evaluate on FuGIBench, a streaming-video benchmark for preparation, response, and cancellation in tool-handover assistance. The best-performing variants of EviBridge-E and EviBridge-I achieve Overall scores of 0.6448 and 0.5892, compared with 0.2178 and 0.5327 for their respective task-adapted native baselines. These gains span target handovers, long waits, and cancelled requests, demonstrating the value of predictive visual evidence for interaction decisions.

类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)

Abstract:Palmprint recognition and synthesis methods focus on extracting discriminative textures or generating images with varied textures and appearances. However, they do not generally provide an explicit image-level representation that separates palmprint texture from its underlying base appearance for independent analysis or controlled editing. We introduce Palmprint Decomposer, an interpretable framework that represents a palmprint through independently editable factors and reconstructs the image through a multiplicative composition model. A color map and a light map characterize the base appearance, while a structure map and a global texture strength parameter describe texture modulation. However, accurate reconstruction alone does not guarantee separation of palmprint texture from base appearance, as fine palmprint textures may leak into the estimated base appearance. To mitigate this ambiguity, we train the decomposer exclusively on synthetic data with direct factor supervision, using asymmetric decoding paths and decomposition constraints to suppress texture leakage. Instance-Wise Refinement further improves real-image reconstruction by directly optimizing the predicted factors for each input without relying on the trained network. Experiments across seven datasets demonstrate high reconstruction fidelity, with the extracted structure maps generally achieving verification performance comparable to the original images. Compared with existing methods, our approach achieves better factor separation while preserving more discriminative palmprint texture information.

[CV-63] Can Image Generators Hold a Scene Together When Space Is Broken Apart?

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20906
作者: Jhen-Ke Lin,Chung-Chun Wang
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 23 pages

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Image generators are good at drawing scenes in which things that belong together appear next to each other. In almost every image they generate, and in almost every benchmark used to evaluate these images, “belonging to the same whole” and “adjacent to each other” go together. Therefore, we cannot know whether the model truly grasps the scene as a whole, or simply makes each part connect with its adjacent parts. We propose GJBench to disentangle the two. It requires the model to draw a scene as a scattered jigsaw puzzle: an image is cut into interlocking pieces, then moved apart and rotated. Thus, the spatial plausibility of the scene exists only in how these pieces collectively point to a whole. The model may have a reference image, a target layout, both, or neither. We separately evaluate three requirements: whether the scene is broken down into a specified number of separate pieces, whether the pieces interlock, and whether the pieces can reconstruct the reference scene. While every open and closed model we evaluated could draw these scenes well as a whole, none could keep them together as scattered puzzle pieces, and the three requirements categorized failures into different patterns. The models draw separate pieces but miscount them in different ways, and unless their outlines are provided, the pieces rarely interlock, and their content does not reconstruct the reference image. We also found that the target layout helps the puzzle pieces fit together, while the reference image improves neither their count nor their fit. These findings show that keeping a scene continuous across space that the canvas no longer shows remains an open problem for image generators.

[CV-64] SciWorldBench: Do Video World Models Really Understand Scientific Experiments?

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20899
作者: Xue Yang,Haonan Cai,Xinyu Hang,Zhimeng Huang,Xuanyi Liu,Chuanmin Jia,Siwei Ma
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: Preprint. Benchmark paper with paired scientific experiments for evaluating video world models. 8 pages of main text, 16 pages including figures and references

点击查看摘要

Abstract:While the ability of video generation models to accurately depict scientific phenomena has received growing attention, determining whether these models genuinely understand the underlying principles remains a critical challenge. Existing benchmarks typically evaluate video samples in isolation, making it difficult to expose models that simply fit superficial visual priors. In scientific experiments, a small change in one condition produces a markedly different outcome even when the rest of the setup remains fixed. Capitalizing on this sensitivity, we introduce SciWorldBench, a benchmark comprising paired scientific experiments. Each pair varies a single condition in an otherwise fixed setup, yielding two mutually exclusive expected outcomes. Each generation prompt specifies the condition but omits the expected outcome. We evaluate ten text-and-image-to-video (TI2V) models using an independent vision-language model (VLM) that assesses each video without access to the condition text or the label identifying the correct outcome. A pair is scored as correct only when both videos depict their respective scientifically correct outcomes. Across all ten models, we find that the two videos in an experimental pair frequently depict the same outcome even though the conditions require different results. This recurring failure suggests that current video world models struggle to apply the underlying scientific principles reliably during generation. We will publicly release the benchmark dataset and open-source the evaluation code.

[CV-65] Certified Not Explained: Exact Token Erasure in Gated Vision State Space Models

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20897
作者: Sadia Parveen,Tehseen Zia
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Machine Learning (cs.LG)
备注: 20 pages, 4 figures

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Vision models built on Mamba are often explained through their selective step size Delta, on the assumption that a token the scan does not admit cannot influence the prediction. We test that in a concept bottleneck model for lung-nodule malignancy built on a single gated, bidirectional selective state-space block. The answer becomes an interpretability framework: a guarantee, a procedure that checks it, and a pre-registered audit of what it explains. For a fixed gate pattern, masking the input of the causal convolution of the block and giving closed tokens zero weight at readout makes the concept and task logits exactly invariant to the closed tokens. Gating Delta is neither necessary nor sufficient. On LIDC-IDRI, a path-by-path knockout over 15 cross-validated models agrees with this in every run: the largest logit change is exactly 0 whenever the conditions hold and between 4.1 and 6.7 when they do not. The gated model reaches a pooled out-of-fold AUROC of 0.8425 +/- 0.0085, level with an ungated Mamba bottleneck (0.8428). The guarantee belongs to the masked model, not to the gate as an explanation. Post-hoc rankers, which inherit the guarantee on this model, order tokens better than the gate. Gate maps from a model trained on permuted labels are as close to the real maps as two real-label seeds are to each other. Under retraining, the tokens of the gate carry more task information than random tokens and, on shifted crops, more than central ones, but no more than the tokens chosen by hidden attention. We therefore read the gate as a certified support set produced by mask supervision. Splitting the Oracle Impurity Score into own-concept and cross-concept parts reveals differences the aggregate score misses. Partitioning the readout reduced leakage slightly under an earlier recipe, and the final model sits at, rather than below, the level implied by correlations among the true concepts.

作者: Jiameng Li,Minye Wu,Matthew B. Blaschko

备注: 8 pages

Abstract:Mixture-of-Experts Multimodal Large Language Models (MoE-MLLMs) offer scalable inference through sparse expert activation, yet substantial computational redundancy remains among the activated experts. Existing expert skipping methods typically calibrate thresholds based on target skipping ratios or final-output divergence, overlooking the accumulation of skipping-induced error across layers and the varying semantic importance of individual tokens. To address that, we propose ProSE, a training-free, semantic-guided expert skipping framework that probes layer-wise reconstruction error to promote representation consistency compared with default activation. Specifically, we construct query-aware semantic masks to identify salient visual tokens and progressively calibrate modality-specific skipping thresholds for each MoE layer. By minimizing masked reconstruction error under a given budget, ProSE maintains semantic consistency after skipping and allows adaptive expert allocation under limited activation budgets. Extensive experiments on 9 benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements on average over existing expert skipping methods, particularly under aggressive skipping settings. ProSE maintains over 96% performance on KimiVL-A3B-Inst with 83% expert skipping and accelerates prefilling by 1.7\times .

[CV-67] Multi-Rate Flow Matching for Point Cloud Upsampling

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20879
作者: Jingkai Shang,Edgar Torres,Duy Nguyen
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Flow-matching point-cloud upsamplers refine sparse inputs into dense point clouds by integrating a learned velocity field with a fixed temporal discretization. However, local reconstruction requirements vary substantially across a shape, while a shared solver budget applies the same temporal resolution everywhere. We propose Multi-Rate Flow Matching (MRFM), a patch-adaptive framework that selects an integration budget for each local patch at inference time while keeping the learned velocity field frozen. MRFM relaxes the discrete budget into a continuous variable, optimizes it online through differentiable soft rollouts using an input-derived geometric fidelity objective, and projects the result back to a discrete budget for the final solver rollout. Experiments on PU1K and PUGAN show strong reconstruction quality, while matched-budget permutation and multi-factor analyses demonstrate that the benefit depends on patch-specific allocation rather than on the step distribution alone. MRFM is accuracy-oriented and intentionally uses additional test-time optimization to obtain more suitable local temporal resolutions.
